speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: After the discussion in Parliament, Mr Leong made a Facebook post about it on Monday night.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Given the nature of some of his statements, which are serious misrepresentations, I had wanted to address them in Parliament yesterday, at the earliest opportunity.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: But out of respect for Mr Leong's bereavement over the passing of his mother, I decided to postpone it, though his post was put up a few hours earlier.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: I also express my deepest condolences to him and I am sure Members will join me in that.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The matter I am going to speak about arises from his post.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Mr Leong's actions are quite improper, as I will show.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: What he has done is wrong and contrary to the requirements of Parliamentary procedure.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: I specifically asked Mr Leong to tell us which parts of the answer he disagreed with.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: He did not respond and we moved on.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Mr Leong makes these allegations and more, but he does not deal with the main points.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Members can refer to the answer I gave on Monday.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Allow me enough time to ventilate, because sometimes, I have to put the thing into context, since I have been specially called back to face the Minister.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: With regard to his question, I have read the Judgment and the opinion of the DT and C3J.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: But I have also been told that the new allegations raised by the Senior Minister and Minister are actually new allegations, like perjury.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I do not know, I am not legally trained.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: And then, on Monday, the Minister talked about absconding.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: So, we asked has a written order been issued?

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Maybe he will give us more information afterwards.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Mr Leong, I believe the Minister has the rest of his Statement.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: He is asking for a specific response to a particular position.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: You will have your chance to ventilate later.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: And the reason why we are doing this is that, in Parliament, when there are issues being raised, we would like the issues to be debated fully here and not in part, and then, thereafter, making statements outside.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: And that is why there is a need for us to discuss the issue now.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: So, perhaps, if you can respond directly to those questions what your views are and then allow the Minister to finish his Statement, and then, we will have ample opportunities for you to say what you need to say.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Yes, but Speaker, I hope you also understand that in this House —

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: If the Member can give me an answer, he can give it to me.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: I think it is subject to legal interpretation.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Okay, if that is your position, then we allow the Minister to carry on.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: So, the Member does not know whether the C3J and DT have said that Mr Lee Hsien Yang and Mrs Lee Suet Fern lied on oath.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Can I take that to be the answer?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Can I ask that through you, Sir, that he does not know?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: He has said what he said, we can leave it to the rest to interpret.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Unless Mr Leong have a response to that?

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Speaker, Sir, that is why this whole issue is not about "if".

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: It is about if you want to raise a new —

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The Member can talk about what he wishes at the end.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: If they lied on oath, is it possible criminal conduct?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Either he knows or he does not know, and we will move on.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Speaker, can I say that I am not going to answer the Minister like answering in Court.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: What is your response to that or no response for the moment?

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: No, what I said just now, Speaker, is that you do not put in new "ifs" or "whats" in this Parliament.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: If you have "ifs" and "whats", let the Court decide.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: That is what we are trying to drive at.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: If there was possible criminal conduct, would the Member accept that that should be properly investigated?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: If I may, it is a question of process. "If something like that were to happen, would that be...?" We are not ascertaining whether, in your views, whether you think they are guilty or not.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I said on Monday, in my summary, that they have essentially absconded from the jurisdiction.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The facts have been stated in Senior Minister Teo's answer on 2 March 2023 and in statements issued by the Police, on 2 and 20 March 2023.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: They said they will tell the Police when they will be available.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Police then handed them a letter providing details of the investigation and the interview.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The blank spaces that Members see were filled in by hand, by the officer.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: So, the form was given with details filled in.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I had said in my response to Ms Sylvia Lim on Monday, that there was an email.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Actually, this form was given and there were email exchanges after that.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: After Senior Minister Teo gave his reply in Parliament on 2 March 2023, Mr Lee Hsien Yang said in a Facebook post on 7 March that he has, I quote, "been made a fugitive by   own country".

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I have asked for his post to be flashed on the screen.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And on 12 March 2023, he reposted in Instagram, his Facebook post that he is a "fugitive".

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And he said in an interview with a foreign news outlet released on 8 March 2023 that he is, quote, "unlikely to return to Singapore, at least for the foreseeable future." He himself admits that he is a fugitive.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: To assist Mr Leong in better understanding the dictionary meaning of "fugitive", I will flash it on the screen and I will just read two.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: From Merriam-Webster: a fugitive is a person who flees or tries to escape, such as a person involved in a criminal case, who tries to elude law enforcement, especially by fleeing the jurisdiction.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Macmillan's definition: someone who has done something illegal and is trying to avoid being caught by the police.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: You can also look at Longman, Oxford, Cambridge.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: This is how Mr Lee describes himself, he says that he has run away to avoid the Police.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: For all we know, they might be in regular contact with each other.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Yes, Mr Lee Hsien Yang is a member of the Progress Singapore Party (PSP).

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: But the real issue here that we are discussing is about fairness and equality before the law.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: It is not about whether he is a member of the PSP or not.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: And whether every citizen is given fair and equal treatment.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Whatever Mr Lee said in his post, when we name a person to have absconded, we must follow our criminal procedure properly.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: So, if you have not issued him a written order, then your process has a problem.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: And you do not have the right to say that he has absconded.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I take it that the Member does not wish to say whether Mr Lee Hsien Yang will come back and cooperate with the authorities.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And, Sir, there is nothing flawed with the process.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Police have explained the process and I repeat, both in this House and I am prepared to repeat it outside, Mr Lee Hsien Yang has absconded, on the facts.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: That is consistent with what Mr Lee Hsien Yang himself has said, that he is a fugitive.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: So, let us not engage in false rhetoric.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I will carry on with my Ministerial Statement.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Everyone, including Mr Leong, knows that they have left the country, that they are "fugitives" and they have told the media they are not returning to Singapore.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: So, let us not hide behind a smoke screen of whether or not a Criminal Procedure Code order was issued.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: They were asked to cooperate and they have run away.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And you can say they have absconded, when they themselves know they are "fugitives".

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: That deals with the two main points I have made.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I told the Member on Monday, I had explained the differences between KOM and the case involving Mr Lee Hsien Yang and Mrs Lee Suet Fern, and why they are different.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I had also explained in my answer on 20 March, why in some circumstances when some names are disclosed in legal proceedings, nevertheless, Police may not release the names here.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I invited him to point out so we can discuss which area of my explanation he does not understand or disagrees with.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: He said there are double standards because the individuals in the KOM case are, I quote his words, "actually guilty".

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: When we want to say that someone is "guilty", I would like to remind all Members to have a care.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Mr Leong has said that persons investigated by the Corrupt Practices Investigation Bureau (CPIB) are, I quote, "actually guilty".

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: That is making assertions against a number of persons, that they are guilty of criminal offences, that they have been found guilty of criminal offences, when in fact, they have not been found guilty.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: I actually was the first to raise the issue that whether the Senior Minister and Minister should make such statements in this Parliament.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: And now, he is turning it around and says that I have made certain statement.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: But I will answer his question first and I hope he answers the question I will ask, fully, later.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: When I say these individuals are guilty, because this is based on the information that we have obtained about what happened overseas, in the overseas jurisdiction.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Is the Member saying they have been found guilty, all of them, in any Court of law?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Or is he otherwise prepared to withdraw his statement?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: If he says he is not prepared to withdraw, we leave it and we follow up.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: I have the impression that they are found guilty in the overseas court of law.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Can I know what is the basis on which the Member says that he is under that impression; that they have all been found guilty?

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: This is based on the case; the case has been such a big case overseas and in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: And the Keppel Corp has paid such a big fine overseas.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Can I suggest that Member works a little bit, finds out what he is talking about, before coming here and making serious allegations?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: If I were to tell him that his statement is false, it is untrue to say that they have all been found guilty elsewhere, certainly not in Singapore, is he prepared to withdraw his statement?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And it is a very serious statement to come here, make allegations without doing your homework and then propagate this sort of stuff – all over the place; really unparliamentary and not acceptable.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And then to say, "Well, I have read", "It seems to be big".

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Unfortunately, this is a thread running through all of Mr Leong's statements.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And that is not the way debates ought to go.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I am glad Mr Leong has withdrawn that statement.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Next, and therefore the basis on which Mr Leong says, "Oh, you know it is similar to this case", it is not there.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And I had given various other reasons why there are differences.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The Member has ascribed an improper motive to me.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The essence of his statement is that I used an example which is irrelevant and that it was used to confuse Parliament.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: If that is what he thought, if he had said it, I would have responded immediately.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: We have no problem, I certainly have no problem with Members challenging me, debating.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The tougher the debate, the better it is, because the public then gets a better sense of which opinion is better or where the facts are.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: But when a statement is made in Parliament and the Member does not respond; and then goes out, and particularly when I said is there anything that you disagree with or you do not understand, and he keeps quiet.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: He keeps quiet and then goes out and says this.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: So, Sir, again, I will have to trouble you.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I seek a clarification from Mr Leong, through you.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: First of all, I want to clarify, in my opinion, that even in our debate in this House, it is not necessary that all the time we have enough time and opportunities to refute every point.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Is he saying I am not telling the truth when I invited Members to respond to me?

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Speaker, I did not say Minister is not saying the truth —

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: I am saying that we may not —

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: On this debate, I expressly invited Members' response.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: I do not think the debate that we had on Monday had lasted long enough.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Mr Leong, if I recall, questions were asked, you did not respond.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: If you had raised your hands to respond, the time would have been given to you to do that.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Well, Speaker, you have a very good memory.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: I had the opportunity to talk two times.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: But I wanted a third time to talk.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: You did not raise your hand to ask.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Before I could raise my hand, it went to another question already.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: We can look at the video because these things are on video now.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I give an opportunity to the Member to correct himself.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: It would be accurate to say that we asked and Member did not respond.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: And if I may add, Mr Leong, are you alleging that I did not give you the time to respond?

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: I am saying that the debate could have been longer.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Because the questions were asked; I was watching whether you had responses.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Because I think I need to clarify for myself.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Are you alleging that I am not permitting you the space to respond?

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Well, Speaker, sometimes, when we are debating an issue like this, it needs time to digest.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Sometimes, it may take a bit of time to respond.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: But when the process just moves through so fast, there will be —

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: We had a debate, exchange, answered his question.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And there being no further questions, the matter, Parliament proceedings moved on.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And can I invite the Member to agree that that is what happened?

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Speaker, I think for the sake of time, let me answer the question about Karl Liew.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: No, I have just said, this is what happened.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Yes, I think probably I was digesting the information at that time.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: So, now I have asked, why does the Member say in his Facebook post that the Parti Liyani case is not relevant?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Why do you say it is not relevant?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I am asking a clarification for Mr Leong on his Facebook post, which suggested the Parti Liyani case that I referred to is not relevant.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And I would like to know from Mr Leong why he says that it is not relevant.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And if he does not know the answer, he can just tell us.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Speaker, I did not say it is not relevant.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: That is, in essence, what "muddy the waters" means.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: So, I want to ask through you, Sir, again, does Mr Leong accept that the Parti Liyani case is relevant?

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Speaker, I do not accept that the Parti Liyani case is relevant for this debate because — Minister, let me finish.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: We can let Mr Leong have a quick response on why it is not relevant.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Minister, in that case, I am not going to answer any more of your question.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I am allowing you the space to elaborate on your response.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: So, because the issue here is about the fairness of the KOM case and the Lee Hsien Yang case.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: So, you do not need to bring in a new case.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: When you bring in a new case, in a way, you are clouding the thinking of people.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: I did not say you are confusing Parliament.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Minister, do not put words into my mouth.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Speaker, now Minister is testing whether I am from a lousy school or not.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: No, Mr Leong, I think the reason is this.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: There are reasons why we have debates in Parliament – so that we can debate the issues here, clarify and so on.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: But when we carry on the debate in a one-dimensional way outside, I think the idea here is to continue that.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Because certain statements are made in your statements.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I think the request is to let us clarify to make sure that we tease out what exactly is the clarity that the public wants to know.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: But, Speaker, I must say, this kind of questioning is not what a legislative chamber should be.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: No, I think if allegations are made in —

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: If allegations are made in Parliament, certain statements are made, I think it is free for Members to question and query.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: So, the question is, you made a statement, out in your Facebook post about "muddy the waters" and the Minister is asking, what exactly do you mean?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: There is no allegation about what school you came from.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I am sure you are from a very good school.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Yes, but the Minister already said that I am saying this because it is irrelevant, I am trying to imply it is irrelevant, I am trying to say that he is confusing the Parliament, which I did not say.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: So, the question he is asking is, what do you mean when you say "muddy the waters".

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: I did not say that you are confusing Parliament.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Can I take it that you say the Parti Lyani case is relevant to the current discussion?

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: "Muddy the waters", in my understanding of English is that, you cloud the real issues.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: That is why you are swimming in the muddy water, you cloud the real issues because you introduce new things into the discussion.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: "You cloud the waters", "you introduce new things" so that people cannot see the facts.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: It is irrelevant and you are introducing it.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Can I ask that question, Sir, for the last time?

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Speaker, I am not going to answer that.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And will the Member accept that it was quite wrong to have suggested motives on a false basis?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Because I have explained why it is relevant.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: You can disagree here, but if you do not disagree, and you keep quiet, and you go out there, then I am entitled to ask this, and say it is not my intention to leave the matters be here, if the Member would not withdraw his allegation.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The Ministerial Statements in 2017 Parliament debates on 38 Oxley Road all took place here in Parliament.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Earlier this month, a question was asked in Parliament on 38 Oxley Road.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I explained on Monday why the matter had to be answered, in response to a Parliamentary Question.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Speaker, I understand that 38 Oxley Road is a matter that is of public interest.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: That, I agree; and even if it was debated in Parliament before the time I came into Parliament, I have no issue with that.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: But when there are further developments to that, especially with regard to the personal behaviours of Mr Lee Hsien Yang and Mrs Lee Suet Fern, I do not think there is a need to raise those issues in Parliament again.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: That is what I am trying to drive at.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Well, then that is a false basis because the issue came about because there was a question that was raised and answers were given.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Parliament is a place where we exchange viewpoints.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And that is why we have to pull it up and ask a number of questions.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: That is why I decided to ask the Member a number of questions.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Because Parliament should not be brought into disrepute with this kind of conduct.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: This is not the first time Mr Leong has breached the rules of parliamentary procedure.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: This has unfortunately become a pattern with Mr Leong.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: In Parliament, we are prepared, as I said, for serious debate.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Members can be as tough as they wish.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And if anyone has questions, they can be raised as we are discussing, rather than keeping quiet here and then, going out and casting aspersions.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: But you do not go out after keeping quiet here and try and mislead the public.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: That is the rationale for section 31, and that is why we have to take a serious view.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Parliament is a place for discussion – I agree entirely with Mr Leong.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: But it is not a place for playing hide and seek.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Speaker, I would only agree to delete my post if the Minister points out specifically again, what are the issues of my post? "Muddying the waters" is not something that is an issue.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Please elaborate again, how does that word "muddy the waters" become an issue.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I went through it, but for his benefit, I will say that again.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I explained why Parti Lyani's case was relevant.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: In that case, the High Court had expressed the view that Mr Karl Liew had not acted honestly and had lied on the witness stand – possible offence of perjury.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: He was being investigated, we disclosed that, here, before it was made public, before he was charged.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: In this case, Mr Lee Hsien Yang and Mrs Lee Suet Fern have been said to have lied on oath – possible offence of perjury.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: If the Member thought that that was not relevant, I am happy for a debate.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I am not saying everyone has got to agree with what I said.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Disagree, explain, debate and so that the public can have a better understanding, if you think it is not relevant.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Keep quiet here, go out and say, "Oh, it's an attempt to muddy the waters", that is casting aspersions on me, that I am doing this to confuse.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Speaker, Sir, I have given my explanation just now, that "muddying the waters" just means that — in my post, I also said, "let us concentrate on the differences between the Lee Hsien Yang and the KOM cases".

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: I am not casting aspersions on the Minister at all.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: That case will actually cloud the judgement of other people, so let us concentrate on the differences between the Lee Hsien Yang and the KOM case – that is the meaning of that.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: We will then proceed to consider what the next steps ought to be.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: If at any time Member changes his mind, before a decision is reached, he can let us know.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Speaker, so, can I confirm that what the Minister has said is that, there are specifically two problems with my post: one is "muddying the waters"; and two, is the statement I made about Senior Minister and himself about using this Parliament to say certain things.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Are those the only two points which the Minister is taking issue with my post?

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Then, I want to explain the second point as well.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Speaker, so my understanding of the processes, of our legal processes is that, when you name someone to have committed perjury or you say someone has absconded, and if the process that we have put in place through our legal system has not been strictly followed, and then you are saying those things in Parliament, is that not something that we should think about, as Members of this House?

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: That is the spirit of what this Parliament should be, that I am trying to write in my post.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Likewise, when we say that he has absconded, when he himself has described himself as a fugitive, it is entirely in order.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: If he is charged for absconding from jurisdiction, he can then explain what he meant.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And, certainly, our statements here are not evidence.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Our statements here are meant to further our discussions, in furtherance of what actually happened.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: When you have run away and you describe yourself as a fugitive, I do not think there is anything wrong in calling you an abscondee, particularly when you have said you will cooperate and then run away without cooperating.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I did not say that they have been charged and found guilty.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: But in any event, Sir, unless there are any other clarifications on my Statement, that is the end of my Statement.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Speaker, I will make this my last question to the Minister.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: So, does the Minister agree that before the due legal process is being followed, Members make statements about, potentially, there may be a criminal behaviour of certain individuals – is that acceptable?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: We do that in a number of situations when we say that people are being investigated, and I have given you a number of illustrations when we said, when we revealed that investigations are ongoing.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: When you say that investigations are ongoing, the implication with it is that, certainly, you are suspected by the Police.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Mr Leong did not think there was anything wrong with that statement being made about Mr Karl Liew.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: He did not think there was anything wrong about Mr Chew when we said that he had attempted to flee the jurisdiction.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I would not say frequently but it has happened a number of times.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And as I said, if you look at it, and if it is a question that is asked here or even outside, Police have released that information.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: But nobody in their right minds will, therefore, think that either the Police or Members here are, therefore, saying that they have been found guilty.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: But that does not mean that we cannot say so and so is being investigated.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: We have to look at the prejudice to the person, possible prejudice, and I have explained in my answer, why there was very little prejudice here, to disclose that they are being investigated.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Likewise, the fact that they have run out of jurisdiction – I mean if you want, we can keep saying each time they have run out of jurisdiction and escaped from the Police.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: We use a short-hand term: they have absconded.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: But did anybody say that they have been found guilty?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: You do look at the prejudice that might be caused when you make statements; you need to be careful.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: But I explained in great detail why there is hardly any prejudice.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: So, that is the crux of the matter that I wanted to debate in this Parliament.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: When it comes to the KOM case, it says "Oh no, we don't need to release the names".

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: So, that gets me, and I wanted to clarify that in this Parliament.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Unless the Member has a specific query or disagrees with my explanation, I do not know how I can answer further.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I mean, I have explained all the differences, why the case is different.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: In fact, his reason for saying that it is the same, one of which is completely false, and he has withdrawn it.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: So, if the Member has a specific reason for disagreeing with the differences I have pointed out, I would invite the Member not to make these allegations that people speak in this way or that way.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Let us keep to the facts; do not be pejorative.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Speaker, I thought I have always been backing up what I have said so far.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: I explained to you what I mean by "muddying the water".

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: I explained to you why I disagree with the inclusion of Karl Liew's example.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: That when Karl Liew's case came up, we have not gotten the KOM case.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: And by the way, I want to make one clarification.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: In my post, I did not mention that the six individuals are guilty, but it is from my Parliamentary statement.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Did you say that the six of them are guilty or not?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And I did say – I think Member pays attention sometimes and he does not pay attention sometimes.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: If I may, Mr Leong, did you withdraw your allegation on the six individuals?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I was not sure whether I have heard it.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Speaker, if Minister did not ask me, I suggest you do not ask me.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: And the tone in which we address one another is important.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: I would, therefore, ask Mr Leong to be mindful of that.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And he withdrew that allegation, which is false, by saying he did not know the facts.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: As for the others, one of the problems with having a discussion with Mr Leong is that: he talks about KOM, I have explained that, I have explained the differences between KOM and here.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And then he says, "Oh, but I have backed up" and he goes on to other things.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And I suggest we leave at that, Sir.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Speaker, I think it is very difficult for public perception or for the public to understand; because I do not understand fully what the Minister had tried to explain about the differences between the two cases.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: I think he raised, basically, three areas: public interest, prejudice and having absconded.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: On public interest, I would think that the KOM case is just as significant in terms of public interest.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: If not, even more than the Lee Hsien Yang case.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: So, is that not a condition that the KOM individuals should be disclosed?

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: But many of us would think that there is even less likelihood of prejudice in the case of the KOM case, when the individuals have already been widely reported overseas.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: So, that is the doubt that every Singaporean and the public of Singapore would have, although you may, technically explain some of the legal details here and there, but the public perception is something that we have to deal with in this House.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: That is why I disagree with what the Minister had explained between the KOM case and the Lee Hsien Yang case.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The harm associated with naming someone when charges would not be pursued, must be weighed.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I would ask Mr Leong and Members to think about this carefully.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Are we saying that in future, if we decide that a case cannot be made out against some persons who have been investigated, let us be clear, are we saying that if a case cannot be made out, we ought to release the names simply because some of their names had been in the media or, in some other place?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Do Members really think it is right to accept the principle that simply because names have been published elsewhere, we proceed to release them here, even when the agencies have concluded that they cannot be prosecuted?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: If Mr Leong is saying that, let me know; if that is the principle that you are suggesting?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: This is a case, the KOM case, where the agencies have concluded, that they cannot proceed with the case.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And in these circumstances, the general policy of not disclosing the names of the individuals who had been investigated, applies.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: It applies to KOM, and it applies to anyone else.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: As I said, one person subsequently pleaded guilty in the United States – the legal counsel.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Then, you assess, do you release his name alone and not the others?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: This is not a case of politicising these matters.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: If you apply it here, then you must be prepared that, in future, whenever some names have been leaked in the media elsewhere or whenever their names have been mentioned in some context, not as defendants, the Court does not express an opinion, their names are mentioned by some witnesses, is Mr Leong arguing for the principle – and I would like to hear from him – that in all such cases, as long as the names are mentioned by someone and are public, then when we investigate, even when we conclude that there is no case, we ought to release the names?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Can I hear from him, through you, Sir?

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Speaker, I think I am not going to answer that question.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Speaker, that is not the principle I am asking.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: But I am saying that if these people in the KOM case have been widely publicised —

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: If you say this is the principle, I will tell the Police, please consider releasing.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And rightly so, because it is very wrong for people's names to be released after the agencies have already concluded that they cannot be charged.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Do you have a fresh perspective, Mr Leong?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Do you have a fresh perspective to add, rather than repeating the same points?

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: I agree with the Minister that we should not release the names, if the case is really closed.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: But we should also apply the same principle – that individuals who have not even been subject to Court proceedings, why are you releasing their names?

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: So, I want that principle to be upheld as well.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The Member agrees with me that the names ought not to be released.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: That is the end of it, Mr Leong.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: No, this is not for you to respond.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Can I just remind you, as illustrated, I have been more than tolerant, more than accommodative of you, on the various occasions for you to speak up.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Can I remind you that, at the very least, let us retain the decorum of this Chamber in terms of whether you are addressing myself or other Members?

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Yes, Speaker, I actually just want to —

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: The Clerk will now proceed to read —

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: The Clerk will now proceed to read the Order of the Day.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Speaker, actually, I want to extend an apology to you.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: I actually want to extend an apology to you.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: But just before that, you said I was "silly" just now?

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Did you say I am trying to say something silly?

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: I apologise to you for what I have said just now, that regarding, if the Minister did not ask the question, please do not ask the question.
